﴿Those are the ones whose hearts God did not desire to purify﴾. In this is evidence against those who deny qadar (divine decree). ﴿For them in this world is disgrace﴾. This refers to the hypocrites and the Jews. As for the disgrace of the hypocrites: their hypocrisy was made manifest in this world. As for the disgrace of the Jews: their distortion was made clear. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 42:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They are listeners to falsehood﴾ (He) mentioned it a second time for emphasis and reinforcement. ﴿Devourers of unlawful gain (suht)﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: it is bribery, and suht is that which is forbidden. He said: "Every flesh that grows from suht, the Fire is more deserving of it." The root meaning of suht is extirpation (isti'sal), so the forbidden is suht, because it uproots blessing. The poet said: "The bite of time, O son of Marwan, has left nothing of wealth except that which is uprooted (musahhat) or stripped bare (mujallaf)."

That is: except wealth in which there is no blessing, and a few things. ﴿So if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: it is abrogated by His saying: ﴿And judge between them by what Allah has revealed.﴾ This was also the view of Mujahid and 'Ikrimah. Al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i said - and this is the view of al-Hasan - that it is not abrogated. Al-Hasan said: there is no abrogated verse in al-Ma'idah. They said: the meaning of His saying, ﴿and if you judge between them, judge by what Allah has revealed﴾ is: if you judge and choose to judge. This is not a binding command; this choice between judging and turning away applies when two dhimmis go to litigation. As for when a Muslim and a dhimmi go to litigation, judgment is obligatory.

It was also said: this choice in judging concerns the rights of Allah, may He be exalted; but as for the rights of human beings, judgment is necessary.

﴿And if you turn away from them, they cannot harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice﴾, i.e., with fairness (al-'adl). ﴿Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.﴾

"His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how would they make you judge while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of Allah?﴾ This is an expression of wonder directed at the Messenger, meaning: how do they seek your judgment, when they claim that they have the Torah, which is the truth, and that you are a liar?

﴿Then they turn away after that.﴾ That is, they are not content with your judgment. ﴿And those are not believers.﴾ That is, they do not affirm you as truthful."

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 44:**

Allah's words, ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which is guidance and light, by which the prophets who submitted (aslamu) judge﴾. That is, they submitted to the command of Allah, as He said to Abraham: ﴿When his Lord said to him, "Submit," he said, "I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds"﴾. That is: I have surrendered to the command of the Lord of the worlds. By this He means the prophets who were sent after Moses, so that they would judge according to the ruling of the Torah.

His words, ﴿for those who were Jews﴾, contain an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir). The intended sense is: "In it is guidance and light for those who were Jews." Then He said: ﴿by which the prophets who submitted, and the rabbis (rabbaniyyun) and the scholars (ahbar), judge﴾.

It was also said that the phrase stays in its place, and its meaning is: the prophets who submitted judge by it over those who were Jews. This is like His words, ﴿For them is the curse﴾, meaning: upon them is the curse. And He said to A'ishah, "Stipulate for them the wala' (patronage)," meaning: upon them is the wala'. This is what al-Nahhas said.

It was also said that there is an ellipsis here, as if He said: "for those who were Jews, over those who were Jews," and one of the two was dropped for brevity.

﴿The rabbaniyyun﴾: Abu Razin said they are the wise scholars. The root of rabbani is "rabb al-'ilm" (lord of knowledge), and the alif and nun were added for emphasis. It was also said that the rabbaniyyun are from among the Christians and the ahbar from among the Jews. It was also said that both are from among the Jews, and that the rabbaniyyun are above the abbar.

Al-Mubarrad said: the word ahbar is derived from tahbir, which means embellishment. From this is the hadith: "A man will come out of the Fire whose ḥibr (beauty) and sibr (appearance) have departed," meaning his goodness and beauty. It was also said that it comes from tahbir in the sense of influence, and from it comes al-hibr (ink). The scholar was therefore called ḥibr because his knowledge influences himself and others, as if he were the knowing and acting scholar. Ḥibr and ḥibr are the same, and its plural is aḥbar.

Al-Farra' said: what I have heard most is ḥibr with a kasra on the ḥa', and its plural is aḥbar.

﴿by what they were entrusted (istuhfizu)﴾, that is, by what they were entrusted with ﴿from the Book of Allah, and they were witnesses to it. So do not fear the people, but fear Me. And do not exchange My signs for a small price﴾.

﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers﴾. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, and this is the view of al-Hasan, said: the verse refers to the polytheists. Ibn 'Abbas said: the verse refers to the Muslims, and by it is meant a lesser disbelief (kufr duna kufr).

Know that the Kharijites use this verse as evidence, saying: whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down is a disbeliever. The people of the Sunnah said: one does not become a disbeliever by abandoning judgment. The verse has two interpretations. The first: whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, rejecting it and denying it, those are the disbelievers. The second: whoever does not judge by all that Allah has sent down, those are the disbelievers, and the disbeliever is the one who abandons judgment by all that Allah has sent down, not the Muslim.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 45:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein that the life is for the life, and the eye for the eye, and the nose for the nose, and the ear for the ear, and the tooth for the tooth, and for wounds is retribution.﴾ It is also read in two ways, from His words: ﴿and the eye for the eye﴾. So it is read with the accusative (naṣb) to its end, and it is read with the nominative (rafʿ).

The retaliation (qiṣāṣ) for the soul and for the limbs was legislated in this verse, and it indicated that this was the ruling of the Torah. ﴿So whoever forgoes it as a charity﴾, meaning: by pardoning from retaliation, ﴿it is an expiation for him.﴾ They differed over whether the pronoun in "for him" refers back to whom? Ibn Mas'ud and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs said: it refers back to the one who was wounded, meaning the pardon. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it refers back to the one who inflicted the injury, as if he regarded the pardon as a kind of exacting from him; so it is an expiation for him just as if retaliation had been carried out against him. ﴿And whoever does not judge by what Allah has sent down, those are the wrongdoers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We sent after them in their footsteps﴾ means: We made to follow in their footsteps. By this He meant the prophets who submitted (aslamu), ﴿[beginning] with Jesus, son of Mary, confirming what was before him of the Torah﴾, meaning: Jesus was confirming the Torah.

﴿And We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light, and confirming what was before it of the Torah, and guidance and admonition for the righteous﴾. Meaning: the Gospel [was] ﴿confirming what was before it of the Torah, and guidance and admonition for the righteous﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein﴾. He means: and We said, "Let the People of the Gospel judge by what Allah has revealed therein. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed, those are the defiantly disobedient (al-fasiqun)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 5, verse 48:

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book in truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what was before it of the Book﴾, meaning all the other revealed books sent before it, ﴿and as a guardian over it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, a trustee over it. Al-Mubarrad (a grammarian) said: its original form is "mu'yaminan" (مؤيمنا), and the hamza was changed into a haa', as one says "arraqtu al-ma'a" and "haraqtuhu" (I poured out the water). Its meaning is "the trustworthy," and it was said: its meaning is "a witness over it." Abu 'Ubayda said: that is, a watchful guardian. The meanings are close to one another, and the meaning of all of them is that every [book] that the Qur'an confirms and whose truthfulness it testifies to is the Book of God, and whatever it does not confirm is not.

Mujahid recited "muhaymanan" with a fatha on the mim, meaning that Muhammad (ﷺ) is a trustee over it. There is a report that 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "When you supplicate to God, then be hayminu," that is, be confident (amanu, "believe/trust"). A poet said:

(Verily, the best of people after Muhammad ... is his successor who is his trustee, in what is known and what is denied.)

He meant Abu Bakr, his trustee and guardian, who follows him in enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong.

﴿So judge between them by what God has sent down, and do not follow their desires, away from the truth that has come to you﴾, that is: do not turn away from what has come to you and follow their desires.

﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a way﴾. Ash-shir'a (the law, the clear path) and al-minhaj (the way) both mean the clear road. Al-Mubarrad said: ash-shir'a is the beginning of the path, and al-minhaj is the continuous path. Know that the laws differ, and each people has its own law: the People of the Torah have a law, the People of the Gospel have a law, and the People of Islam have a law. As for the religion, it is one in all of them, and it is monotheism (tawhid).

﴿Had God willed, He would have made you one community, but He tests you in what He has given you; so race to the good deeds﴾, that is: hasten to good deeds. ﴿To God is your return, all together, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that you judge between them by what Allah has revealed, and do not follow their desires, and beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you﴾. It has been said: the occasion of the revelation of this verse is that a group of the leaders of the Jews came to the Prophet and said: "O Muhammad, if we believed in you, others would believe in you as well. We have disputes among the people, so rule in our favor against them; we will believe in you, and others will follow us." Their intention was not faith in him; they only intended deception and to invite him to judge by inclination. So the verse was revealed.

﴿And beware of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. But if they turn away﴾, that is, if they refuse, ﴿then know that Allah only intends to afflict them for some of their sins﴾. It has been said: its meaning is "for all their sins," so He expressed the whole by the part. It has also been said: its meaning is that He afflicts them for some of their sins in this world. ﴿And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 50:

As for His saying: ﴿Do they then seek the judgement of the Days of Ignorance?﴾ it is read with the yāʾ (yaghūnā, "they seek") and with the tāʾ (tabghūn, "you seek"), and their meaning is one. That is, when they are not content with the judgement of God and they intend the opposite of the judgement of God, they have sought the judgement of the Jāhiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). Al-Ḥasan, Qatādah, al-A'mash and al-A'raj read: ﴿afaḥukma al-jāhiliyyah﴾ with the meaning of "the judge" (al-ḥākim). Yabghūn: they seek. ﴿And who is better than God in judgement for a people who are certain?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another﴾. It is said: it was revealed concerning ʿUbada ibn al-Samit and ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, who disputed. ʿUbada said: "I disavow the Jews and do not take them as allies." ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy said: "I take them as allies and do not disavow them, for I fear misfortune turning against us." So the verse was revealed.

It is also said: it was revealed concerning Abu Lubaba ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) sent to Banu Qurayza when he besieged them. They consulted him about coming down (from their fortresses), and said: "What will he do with us if we come down?" He gestured to them toward slaughter, placing his finger on his throat, meaning: he will kill you. He did this out of sincere counsel to them.

It is also said: it was revealed concerning the day of Uhud. When the battle of Uhud ended and the Muslims suffered what they suffered, some people of Madina said: "We will take the Jews as allies," and some of them said: "We will take the Christians as allies, for we fear that the affair of Muhammad will not be completed and that the matter will turn against us." So the verse was revealed: ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies; they are allies of one another. Whoever among you takes them as allies is one of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾.

(And those who believe will say) meaning: [to the Jews], when the condition of the hypocrites was exposed: ﴿Are these the ones who swore by God with their most solemn oaths that they were with you? Their deeds have come to nothing, and they have become losers.﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 54:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, whoever among you reverts from his religion⁠—﴾ And the people of Madina and Syria recited "man yartadid" (whoever reverts), and the meaning is one. ﴿then Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him⁠﴾. Ali and al-Hasan said: this was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and his companions. Al-Hasan used to swear to this, that it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and his companions. That was because when the Prophet (ﷺ) departed to the mercy of Allah, the Arabs apostatised, and Islam remained only in three mosques: the Mosque of Makkah, the Mosque of Madina, and the Mosque of Bahrain. Abu Bakr resolved on fighting, and the Companions disliked that and said: some of them have withheld the zakat, but they have not abandoned the prayer. Abu Bakr said: "By Allah, I will fight whoever separates the prayer from the zakat." It was also said that he drew his sword, went out alone, and said: "I will fight alone." Then the Companions agreed with him. Ibn Mas'ud said: "We disliked that from you at the beginning, then we praised you for it in the end." Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said: I heard Abu Husayn say: "No child has been born after the prophets who is more excellent than Abu Bakr. He stood in the position of one of the prophets"—meaning in fighting the people of apostasy and returning them to Islam.

And Iyad al-Ash'ari narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse, ﴿then Allah will bring a people⁠﴾, and gestured towards Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and said: "This one and his companions." They were from the people of Yemen, and the people of Yemen have a great standing in the conquests that took place in Islam. It has been authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Faith is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." It was also said: he meant by the verse a people most of whom were from the people of Yemen, who conquered al-Qadisiyya in the time of Umar. The first view is more sound.

﴿humble towards the believers⁠﴾: this is not from "dhull" (humiliation) but from "dhilla," which is gentleness. And His words ﴿mighty against the disbelievers⁠﴾: this is not from "izz" (might) but from "izza," which is harshness. That is, their side is gentle towards the believers and stern towards the disbelievers. Ibn Mas'ud recited: "humble towards the believers, harsh towards the disbelievers," and this is the meaning of the well-known reading.

﴿They strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of any blamer⁠﴾: that is, they do not fear the blame of people regarding Allah. Ibn Mas'ud narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever desires Paradise without doubt, let him not fear the blame of any blamer regarding Allah." ﴿That is the bounty of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing⁠﴾.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Your guardian is only Allah and His Messenger⁠﴾. This refers back to His words: ﴿Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies⁠﴾. When He forbade them from allying with the Jews and the Christians, He called them to ally with Allah and His Messenger.

﴿And those who have believed, who establish the prayer and give zakat while bowing⁠﴾: that is, while praying; however, He specified bowing as an honour. It was also said: its meaning is "submitting." Al-Suddi—and this is a narration from Mujahid—said: this was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, who was bowing (in prayer) when a needy man was walking in the mosque, so he removed his ring and gave it to him. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and give zakat while bowing⁠﴾. And from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, who said: the verse was revealed concerning the believers. He was told: "Some people say the verse was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib." Abu Ja'far said: "Ali is among the believers."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 55:

And His saying: ﴿Your walī (guardian, protector) is only Allah and His Messenger﴾ — by it He intends walāya in religion, not the walāya of rulership and sovereignty, and they are above every walāya. Abū ʿUbayda said: Likewise is the meaning of his saying: "Whoever I am mawlā (master, patron) to, ʿAlī is his mawlā," meaning: whoever I am walī to, I help him and support him; so ʿAlī helps him and supports him in religion.
His saying: ﴿And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies, then indeed the party of Allah, they are the victorious.﴾ That is: the soldiers of Allah are the victorious,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take those who have taken your religion as ridicule and play [from] those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers as allies﴾. This is about the Jews. When they heard the muezzin (the one who calls to prayer), they would laugh and exchange winks among themselves. ﴿From those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ means the Jews. ﴿And the disbelievers﴾ means all the other disbelievers. ﴿As allies﴾, meaning: do not take these people as allies.

Al-Kisa'i and Abu 'Amr read "wal-kuffar" (والكفار) with a kasra on the letter ra' (الراء), meaning "and from the disbelievers." Likewise, in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is "and from the disbelievers as allies" (﴿ومن الكفار أولياء﴾). ( ﴿And fear Allah, if you are believers﴾.

(And when you call to the prayer, they take it as mockery and play.) This explains their taking the religion as mockery in the first verse: ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

In the reports: a certain hypocrite called Dammura heard the muezzin call the adhan and said, "May God burn the liar." One night his servant brought him a lamp, and a spark from the lamp fell without his (noticing) it, and he burned along with everything in the house.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 59:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?﴾ That is: do you dislike us? ﴿except that we believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient﴾. That is: do you resent us except for our belief and your wickedness? The poet said:

(They resented nothing of the Banu Umayyah except that ... they would carry (?) when they were angry)

(And they are the lords of kings, and none is fit to be (ruler) except the Arabs over them)

That is: they disliked the Banu Umayyah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 60:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as requital from Allah?﴾ That is: Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that in reward and consequence with Allah?" ﴿Those whom Allah cursed and upon whom He became angry﴾ meaning: the Jews. ﴿And made of them apes and swine﴾ It has been said: Allah made the apes from among the Jews and the swine from among the Christians. Those whom He made apes from among the Jews were the People of the Sabbath (Ashab al-Sabt), and those whom He made swine from among the Christians were the People of the Table (Ashab al-Ma'idah). It has also been said: both groups were from among the Jews, so He made their youth apes and their elders swine. ﴿And served the Taghut﴾ That is: and whoever served the Taghut, meaning: those whom Allah cursed and whoever served the Taghut. Hamzah recited "wa-'abada al-taghut" with a damma on the ba' in 'abada and a kasra on the ta' in al-taghut, and the meaning is one. The poet said:

(Abni Lubayna, in truth your mother... is a servant-girl, and in truth I am your father, a servant)

That is: "like 'a'bad" (i.e., the form is read as a plural of 'abd, servant). It has been said that this is an error on Hamzah's part, but the first (reading) is more sound. In the non-canonical readings it is read "wa-'ibad al-taghut" and "wa-'abadat al-taghut." Its estimated sense is: "and made of them servants of the Taghut," and all of them are the same in meaning.

﴿Those are worse in position and further astray from the right way﴾ That is: from the path of truth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 61:

Allah's saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when they come to you, they say, "We believe"﴾. It has been said: this verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews who entered upon the Prophet and said, "We have believed in you and affirmed what you have said," while they were concealing disbelief. So the verse was revealed: ﴿And when they come to you﴾, meaning: those people say, "We believe," ﴿while they have entered with disbelief and they have left with it﴾, meaning: they entered as disbelievers and they left as disbelievers. ﴿And Allah knows best what they were concealing﴾.

"Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And you see many of them hastening into sin and transgression and their consuming of what is unlawful.﴾ It was said: "al-ithm" (sin) means the acts of disobedience, and "al-'udwan" (transgression) means injustice. And it was said: "al-ithm" means concealing the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what they concealed of the Torah, and "al-'udwan" means what they added to the Torah. ﴿And their consuming of as-suht (unlawful gain)﴾: we have already explained the meaning of as-suht, and as-suht has two dialects (lughatan). It was said: he meant by it their consuming of riba (usury). ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to do.﴾"

His words: ﴿Why do the rabbis and the scholars not forbid them from uttering sin and consuming what is unlawful?﴾ That is, "Why do the rabbinical scholars not forbid them?" We have already mentioned the meaning of rabbaniyyun (rabbinical scholars, those devoted to the Lord). It has also been said that it is a nisba (relative adjective) derived from "Rabb" (Lord), like al-Bahrani being derived from al-Bahrayn and al-Najrani from Najran. ﴿Evil indeed is what they used to do.﴾ In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is "ya'malun" (they used to work/do), and both mean the same thing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Jews say: "Allah's hand is chained up."﴾ The reason for this: the Jews were in abundance and plentiful provision before the Hijra of the Prophet. When he emigrated to Medina, Allah restricted their provision, so the Jews said: "Allah's hand is chained up," meaning: withholding, not spending. It is as if they attributed to Him stinginess. Al-Hasan said: they meant by it, "Allah's hand is chained up, so He does not punish us [with it]." ﴿Chained up are their own hands﴾: Allah, exalted is He, answers them, saying: "I am the Generous, and they are the stingy; their hands are the chained-up, withholding ones." This is what al-Zajjaj said. It was also said: its meaning is that they will be punished on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And they are cursed for what they said﴾: among the forms of this curse is that they were transformed into apes and swine, and among the forms of their being cursed is that humiliation and the jizya (poll tax) were imposed upon them.

﴿Rather, both His hands are outstretched; He spends as He wills﴾: meaning, the two hands of Allah are outstretched; He provides and spends according to His will, as He pleases. The people of knowledge said: there is no refutation in this of the Jews in their affirming a hand for Allah, exalted is He; rather, the refutation of them is in their attributing to Him stinginess. As for the hand, it is an attribute of Allah, exalted is He, without how, and He has two hands. It has been authentically reported from the Prophet that he said: "Both his hands are right hands." And Allah knows best the modality of what is meant.

﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief﴾: in the sense that whenever a verse was revealed, they disbelieved in it, and their transgression and disbelief increased. ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾: it was said: among the sects of the Jews; and it was said: between the Jews and the Christians. His saying, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, is evidence that Judaism and Christianity will remain until near the Hour. ﴿Every time they kindle the fire of war, Allah extinguishes it﴾: the meaning of this: whenever they gathered to corrupt the affair of Muhammad, Allah scattered their gathering and dispersed their unity. ﴿And they strive upon the earth in corruption, and Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And if the People of the Book had believed﴾ in Muhammad ﴿and feared Allah﴾, meaning: refrained from sins, ﴿We would have removed from them their misdeeds and admitted them to Gardens of Bliss﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 66:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was sent down to them from their Lord﴾, meaning: if they had stood by and acted upon what is in the Torah, what is in the Gospel and what is in the Qur'an, ﴿they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet﴾. It has been said: "from above them" refers to the rain of the sky, and "from beneath their feet" refers to the growth of the earth. It has also been said: "from above them and from beneath their feet" means that provision would be made abundant for them. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj, the grammarian and exegete) said, and this is similar to the saying of one who says: "So-and-so is in good from the crown of his head to the sole of his foot," meaning that good was made abundant for him. It has also been said: it is possible that what is meant by His saying ﴿from above them﴾ is from the trees, and ﴿from beneath their feet﴾ is from the plants. It is also possible that what is meant by ﴿from above them﴾ is from the earnings of their forefathers, and ﴿from beneath their feet﴾ is from the earnings of their sons. This is similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if the people of the towns had believed and been mindful of God, We would have opened for them blessings from the heaven and the earth﴾, and similar to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they had gone straight upon the path, We would have given them abundant water to drink﴾. ﴿Among them is a moderate community﴾, meaning: upright, ﴿but many of them—evil is what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 67:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Messenger, proclaim what has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. ʿĀʾisha said: "Whoever claims that Muhammad concealed any part of the revelation has indeed committed a great slander. And whoever claims that Muhammad saw his Lord on the night of the Mi'raj has indeed committed a great slander, for God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾." The report is in the Sahih.

﴿And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message﴾. In this there are two meanings. The first: its meaning is, if you do not convey all of it and leave out one part, then you have conveyed nothing; that is, your offence in abandoning the proclamation of one part is like your offence in abandoning the whole. It was also said: its meaning is, "Proclaim what has been revealed to you," that is, make its proclamation manifest. This is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾, and "if you do not" means: if you do not make its proclamation manifest, ﴿then you have not conveyed His message﴾, ﴿and God will protect you from the people﴾. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Before the revelation of this verse, the Prophet used to have people come to him to guard him. When this verse was revealed, he put his head out and said: 'Disperse, for God will protect me.'" Muhammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazi said: The verse was revealed concerning a disbeliever who drew his sword, intending to kill the Prophet, but the sword fell from his hand, and he began striking his own head against a tree until his brain was scattered. ﴿Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 68:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "O People of the Scripture, you are not upon anything until you uphold the Torah and the Gospel and what has been revealed to you from your Lord."﴾ That is: act upon all of them. ﴿But what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in rebellion and disbelief.﴾ That is what we have mentioned. ﴿So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ That is: do not be sorrowful.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 69:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians﴾. Al-Kisa'i and the grammarians of Kufa said: its implied construction is: "they, and the Sabeans [...]". Sibawayh said: in the verse there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir, transposition of words), and its construction is: "Indeed, those who believed, and those who were Jews, and the Christians — whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness, there is no fear for them, nor will they grieve — and the Sabeans likewise."

And His saying: ﴿whoever believed in Allah﴾ means: those who believed with the tongue; whoever among them believed with the heart. And it was said: "Indeed, those who believed" refers to those who believed in the true sense of faith.

And His saying: ﴿whoever believed in Allah﴾ means: whoever remained steadfast upon faith in Allah. As for the case of the Jews, the Christians and the Sabeans, it is to be understood as true faith.

God, the Exalted, says: "We certainly took the covenant of the Children of Israel" (5:70). We have already mentioned the covenant. "And We sent to them messengers. Every time a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a party they called liars" (5:70). He means: Jesus and Muhammad (ﷺ). "And a party they killed" (5:70). He means: Zechariah and John (Yahya).

And His saying: ﴿And they thought there would be no trial﴾, meaning: punishment. ﴿So they became blind and deaf; then Allah turned to them in forgiveness﴾, meaning: they became blind and deaf after Moses, then Allah turned to them in forgiveness by sending Jesus. ﴿Then many of them became blind and deaf again﴾ by disbelieving in Muhammad. ﴿And Allah is Seeing of what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 72:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly those who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary," have disbelieved.﴾ We have already mentioned the meaning of al-Masih (the Messiah). Al-Nakha'i said: He was named Masih because he would travel over (yamsah) the earth. As for the Dajjal (the Antichrist), he is also called al-Masih, and a report has come that he is called Masih without qualification. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "The Masih will come from the direction of the east, and his aim is Medina." And it occurs in a report: "al-Masih al-Dajjal." And the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "The terror of al-Masih al-Dajjal will never enter Medina."

﴿And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire.﴾ Abu Sufyan Talhah ibn Nafi' narrated from Jabir that the Prophet was asked, "What are the two destinies?" He said: "Whoever affirms the oneness of Allah, associating nothing with Him, will be granted Paradise, and whoever associates others with Allah will be granted the Fire." ﴿And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 73:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Certainly they have disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three."﴾ There is an ellipsis in it, meaning: "the third of three gods." This estimation (taqdir) is necessary, because it is permissible to say "He is the third of three," as He said: ﴿There is not a private conversation of three but that He is their fourth.﴾ And His words, ﴿the third of three﴾, refer to their saying: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. This is the view of the Ya'qubiyya (Jacobites) among them, and they said: the Holy Spirit is neither He nor other than He, and likewise the Son; and Allah is the totality of all of them. ﴿And there is no god except one God. And if they do not desist from what they say, there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment.﴾ That is, there will surely befall those who disbelieved among them a painful punishment.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Will they not turn in repentance (tawbah) to Allah and seek His forgiveness?﴾ He directed them to repentance (tawbah) and Islam (submission to Allah) ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 5, verse 75:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was no more than a messenger; messengers had passed away before him﴾. That is, they had gone by (madat). The past days are called khaliyah (empty, bygone) because they have passed. The meaning is: We sent 'Isa just as We sent others, and We gave him miracles just as We gave other messengers. ﴿And his mother was a siddiqah﴾. The siddiq (truthful) is one who is very truthful; it is an intensive form. From this, Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) was named al-Siddiq. It is also said that he was named siddiq because it was said to him: "Your companion claims that he was taken up by night to the heavens," and he said: "If he said that, then he has spoken the truth."

﴿They both used to eat food﴾. That is, they were nourished by food. The meaning is that one who is nourished by food cannot be a god to be worshipped. Ibn Qutaybah said: this is a metaphor for defecation (al-hadath, i.e., the natural bodily functions). That is, they both eat, drink, urinate and defecate, and such a one cannot be a god to be worshipped. ﴿Look how We make the signs clear to them; then look how they are turned away﴾. Ibn Qutaybah said: this is among the most subtle of expositions. His words ﴿they are turned away﴾ mean they are diverted, and from this falsehood is called ifk (a turning away), because it is turned away from the truth.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Do you worship, instead of Allah, that which possesses neither harm nor benefit for you?﴾ He means: Jesus and the like of him. ﴿And Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 77:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion beyond the truth﴾. Al-ghuluw (excess): transgressing the limit, and it is blameworthy. Likewise is al-taqsir (negligence/falling short). The religion of God lies between excess and negligence. ﴿And do not follow the desires of a people﴾. Al-ahwa' (desires) is the plural of al-hawa (desire), spelled with a short alif (hawa, not hawa'). As for al-hawa'  (with a long alif, spelled with a hamza), it means the air/atmosphere. Al-hawa (desire) is everything to which the appetite of the soul calls, not evidence (al-hujjah). ﴿They had already gone astray before and led many astray, and they strayed from the sound way﴾. If it is said: what is the meaning of this repetition? Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning of His saying ﴿they strayed from the sound way﴾ is that they went astray by misleading others, while the first [going astray] was from straying itself. It was also said: they went astray before misleading [others], and they went astray after misleading [others]; so it is as if they went astray twice.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 78:

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Those among the Children of Israel who disbelieved were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, son of Mary.﴾ Those who were cursed by the tongue of David are the People of the Sabbath (ashab al-sabt), and those who were cursed by the tongue of Jesus are the People of the Table (ashab al-ma'idah). Those are the ones whom God transformed into apes, and these are the ones whom God transformed into swine. ﴿That is because they disobeyed and used to transgress.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They did not forbid one another from the wrong they committed. Evil indeed was what they used to do.﴾ Al-tanahi (mutual forbidding) is a form of tafa'ul from al-nahy (prohibition). Al-munkar (the reprehensible) is everything the Shari'ah has disapproved of. In a report he said: "The first deficiency to enter the Children of Israel was that a man among them would forbid his companion from some wrong, and then this would not prevent him from being his companion, his table-mate, and his drinking-partner. So Allah, exalted is He, struck some of their hearts with others, and included them all in the punishment." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you must either seize the wrongdoer by the hand and turn him firmly to the truth (ta'tiruhu 'ala al-haqq itran), or..." Meaning: you must bend him (ta'tifuhu).

﴿Thou seest many of them making allies of those who disbelieve.﴾ That is, they take them as allies (yuwaliyunahum).

﴿Evil is that which their souls have sent forth before them, that Allah became wrathful against them, and in torment they will abide.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 81:

"If they had believed in God, and the Prophet, and what was sent down to him, they would not have taken them as allies (awliya'), meaning: the disbelievers." ﴿But many of them are defiant transgressors.﴾ If it is said: Why did He call them defiant transgressors (fasiqin) when they are disbelievers? It is said: its meaning is: "departing" (kharijun) from the command of the Lord, and the disbelievers depart from all of His command. And it is said: its meaning is: rebellious (mutamarridun), i.e., they, together with their disbelief, are rebellious.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 5, verse 82:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿You will surely find the most intense of people in enmity toward those who believe to be the Jews and those who associate partners with God﴾, meaning: the polytheists of Mecca. ﴿And you will surely find the nearest of them in affection toward those who believe to be those who say, "We are Christians"﴾. It has been said: the verse was revealed concerning a group of Christians, forty men: thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight monks from Syria. They came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and they embraced Islam, and the verse was revealed concerning them, not concerning the disbelieving Christians, for they are in enmity toward the Muslims like the Jews.

It has also been said: those among the Abyssinians who embraced Islam included al-Najashi (the Negus). Ja'far al-Tayyar came to Abyssinia, and al-Najashi invited him, and he recited to him Surah Maryam, and the bishops and monks were present; they wept until their beards were wet. Al-Najashi took a straw in his hand and said: "Jesus did not exceed what you have said, nor even this much." And they embraced Islam.

It has been said: the verse was revealed concerning a group of Christians who held firmly to the religion of Jesus without altering it, and they believed in Muhammad.

It has also been said: it refers to all Christians, and its meaning is that they are gentler in enmity than the Jews.

﴿That is because among them are priests (qissisin) and monks, and because they are not arrogant﴾. Qatrab said: the *qissis* means the worshipper in the language of the Romans, and it means "the complete" in the language (of the Arabs). The poet said:

(They walk, of a priest's talk, unaware... except *ja'bariyat*, and not *tahamalij*)

The *ruhban* is the plural of *rahib* (monk). Salman narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) recited: "That is because among them are *siddiqin* (truthful ones) and monks," and this is among the strange reports.

Almighty Allah's statement: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger﴾ means: the Qur'an, for the Prophet had recited the Qur'an to them, so they wept and embraced Islam. That is the meaning of His statement: ﴿You see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognised of the truth. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so inscribe us among the witnesses."﴾ means: from the community of Muhammad, for they are the witnesses over all the other nations.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth?﴾ This was because the Jews said: "Why would you [i.e., the Muslims] believe?" So they [the Christians/believers] replied: "And why should we not believe in Allah and in what has come to us of the truth, and [why should we not] hope that our Lord will admit us along with the righteous people?" Al-ṭamaʿ (hope, desire): it is the soul's attachment to a thing together with strong longing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verses 85–86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens﴾, meaning: Allah gave them, for what they said, gardens ﴿beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the reward of the good-doers﴾.

If it is said: this is the first part of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said﴾, on the basis that faith is a single statement [of the tongue alone].

It is answered: He has mentioned in the first verse ﴿of what they recognised of the truth﴾, so He mentioned recognition (ma'rifa) in that verse, and the statement in this verse, and their combination is faith. ﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verses 85–86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens﴾, meaning: Allah gave them, for what they said, gardens ﴿beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. That is the reward of the good-doers﴾.

If it is said: this is the first part of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So Allah rewarded them for what they said﴾, on the basis that faith is a single statement [of the tongue alone].

It is answered: He has mentioned in the first verse ﴿of what they recognised of the truth﴾, so He mentioned recognition (ma'rifa) in that verse, and the statement in this verse, and their combination is faith. ﴿But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 87:

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ [and Saʿd], Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and al-Suddi said: The occasion of the revelation of the verse was that ʿAli, Ibn Masʿud, and ʿUthman ibn Maz'un consulted together about adopting monasticism (tarahhub), wearing woollen garments (masuh), cutting off their genitals (madhakir), and fasting all the time. When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "As for me, I sleep and I pray, I break my fast and I fast, I eat and I drink, and I marry. Whoever turns away from my sunnah is not of me." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you﴾.

It is also narrated that ʿUthman ibn Maz'un said: "O Messenger of Allah, permit me to adopt monasticism (rahbaniyya)." He said: "The monasticism of my community is sitting in the mosques." He said: "Permit me to travel through the earth (siyaha)." He said: "The travelling of my community is jihad in the way of Allah." He said: "Permit me to castrate myself (ikhsa')." He said: "The castration of my community is fasting."

It has also been said that the occasion of the revelation was that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am aroused by meat, so I desire women, and so I have made meat unlawful for myself." Then He, [exalted is He], revealed: {Do not prohibit the good things that Allah has made lawful for you, and do not transgress; indeed Allah does not love the transgressors}. ʿIkrima narrated this from Ibn ʿAbbas.

Al-iʿtida' (transgression) is going beyond what is permitted to what is not permitted for oneself.
﴿And eat of what Allah has provided for you, lawful and good; and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.﴾ He reinforced that prohibition with this command.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 89:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah will not hold you accountable for the unintentional oaths in your oaths﴾. He placed this verse right after the preceding one because the people who had agreed to become ascetics had sworn oaths; so He explained the ruling on oaths. Laghw (unintentional, idle speech) is that which is discarded and not given any weight. It is reported from ʿA'isha that the laghw of an oath is a person's saying: "No, by Allah," and "Yes, by Allah." This was the view chosen by al-Shafiʿi. Ibn ʿAbbas and Abu Hurayra said: the laghw of an oath is that a person swears to something believing it to be so, and then it turns out to be the opposite. The scholars differed concerning whether expiation (kaffara) is obligatory for the oath of laghw. Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi said: expiation is obligatory for it. His saying ﴿will not hold you accountable﴾ means: on the Day of Resurrection. All the other scholars hold that there is no expiation for the oath of laghw, based on the apparent meaning of the Qur'an: ﴿but He will hold you accountable for what you have deliberately bound with oaths﴾. In this verse there are three readings. ﴿ʿaqqadtum﴾ with a light pronunciation is the reading of al-Kisa'i, Hamza and Abu Bakr. ﴿ʿaqqadtum﴾ with a doubled ʿayn is read by Abu ʿAmr and others, except Ibn Dhakwan. ﴿ʿaqadtum﴾ with an alif (ʿaqadtum, from the form of mutual binding) is the reading of Ibn ʿAmir according to the narration of Ibn Dhakwan.

Al-Kisa'i said: ʿaqqadtum means awjabtum, "you made obligatory." Abu ʿAmr said: ʿaqqadtum means wakkadtum, "you confirmed/emphasized." They differed about what this emphasis is. Ibn Jurayj said: I asked ʿAta' about His saying ﴿ʿaqqadtum﴾, what is it? He said: it is the saying of the speaker: "By Allah, there is no god but Him"; as if he explained the emphasis by it. Nafi' reported from Ibn ʿUmar that the emphasis of an oath is by repetition. Nafi' said: when Ibn ʿUmar emphasized an oath, he would free a slave, and when he did not emphasize it, he would feed the poor in its expiation. ﴿So its expiation is feeding ten needy persons﴾. According to al-Nakhaʿi's view, this refers to the oath of laghw; according to the view of the others, it refers to the binding oath, which is the intended one. The binding of an oath is the intention in the heart and the mention by the tongue. ﴿From the average of what you feed your families﴾. Ibn ʿUmar said: the average is bread and olive oil, or bread and dates. ʿUbayda al-Salmani said: it is bread and ghee. Abu Razin said: it is bread and vinegar; as for the higher: it is bread and meat, and the lower: it is plain bread; and all are sufficient. The average in quantity: Zayd ibn Thabit, ʿA'isha and Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them) said it is the mudd, and al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him) said likewise; that is a ratl and a third. ʿUmar and ʿAli (and it is a narration from Ibn ʿAbbas) said it is two mudds, half a ṣaʿ, and the Iraqis held this view.

﴿Or clothing them﴾. ʿAta' and Tawus said: a garment for each needy person. Mujahid said: whatever falls under the name of clothing. Ibrahim said: a comprehensive garment for each needy person suitable for night and day, such as a cloak, a wrap, and the like. Ibn ʿUmar said: three garments. It was also said: two garments, which is the view of al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin, such as a waist-wrap and a shawl, or a waist-wrap and a turban. It was also said: whatever covers the nakedness and with which prayer is valid.

The sound view is that what is obligatory for each needy person is what is suitable as clothing according to custom. ﴿Or freeing a neck﴾, that is, freeing a slave, and there is discussion of this in jurisprudence.

﴿So whoever does not find [means], then a fast of three days﴾. The apparent meaning is that it is permissible to fast them separately, which is the more correct view. Ibn Masʿud and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read: "three days consecutive." On this basis, consecutiveness is obligatory; this is the view of Malik, al-Awza'i, and one of al-Shafiʿi's two opinions. ﴿That is the expiation of your oaths when you swear﴾. It was said: the breaking of the oath is implied in it, meaning: when you swear and break it; expiation is not obligatory except after breaking the oath, and as for the permissibility of paying the expiation before breaking it, we know it from the Sunnah. ﴿And guard your oaths﴾. Its apparent meaning is a prohibition against breaking them. It was also said: it means guarding the oath, that one should not swear at all; but the first is more correct. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His verses, that you may be grateful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 90:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone altars, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.﴾ As for intoxicants (khamr), the discussion of them has already passed, and likewise gambling (maysir). Al-Asma'i said: Their gambling (maysir) was over the camel (jazur). They would buy a camel, slaughter it, and divide it into twenty-eight shares (sahm), and it is said: into ten shares. Then they would cast lots over it. Whoever's arrow emerged would receive his share without payment, while the price would fall upon the rest. They would continue casting lots over each share in this way until one remained, so the entire price would fall upon him, while the others won their shares without payment.

Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad was asked about backgammon (nard) and chess (shatranj): Are they from gambling (maysir)? He said: Whatever diverts from the remembrance of Allah and from the prayer, it is from gambling.

His saying: ﴿And stone altars (ansab) and divining arrows (azlam) are defilement﴾. As for the stone altars and the divining arrows, we have already explained them. His saying: ﴿defilement (rijs)﴾ means: filthy and loathsome. In a report: "I seek refuge with Allah from the rijs, the impure (najs)." ﴿From the work of Satan﴾ means: from the adornment of Satan. ﴿So avoid it that you may be successful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 91:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred to arise among you through intoxicants and gambling﴾. As for the arising of enmity through intoxicants: when its drinkers become intoxicated, they act violently, quarrel, and dispute with one another (and wrangle).

As for enmity through gambling: Qatadah said: It is that they used to gamble away their families and wealth. Then, when nothing remained for him, he would sit down plundered, bereft, and enraged at his companions (in the game). ﴿And it hinders you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer﴾, meaning: Satan prevents you through them from the remembrance of Allah (and from prayer). ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ Its meaning: cease. Al-Farra' said: I heard some Bedouins say to another: "Are you silent? (Are you silent?)" meaning: "Be silent," and this is the speech of the pure Arabs (al-'Arabiyyah al-'aribah).

The occasion of revelation of the verse: "Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'O Allah, make clear to us a sufficient explanation regarding intoxicants.' Then there was revealed (his statement) in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿They ask you about intoxicants and gambling﴾. 'Umar summoned him and recited it to him. He said a second time: 'O Allah, make clear to us a sufficient explanation regarding intoxicants.' Then there was revealed His statement in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated﴾. He recited it to him. He called a third time and said: 'O Allah, make clear to us a sufficient explanation regarding intoxicants.' Then this verse was revealed. He called him and recited it to him. When he reached His statement: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾ he said: 'We have desisted, O Lord.'"

It has also been said: the occasion of revelation of the verse was that Qudamah ibn Maz'un prepared a banquet, roasted the head of a camel, and invited Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas and a group. They ate and drank, and when they became intoxicated they boasted. A man from the Ansar rose to the jaw of the camel and struck Sa'd's face with it, so that his nose was injured. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this verse was revealed.

[It has also been said: it was revealed] concerning two tribes of the Ansar who quarrelled while intoxicated.

Reports about intoxicants have also come down, among them his statement (ﷺ): "The habitual drinker of intoxicants is like a worshipper of idols." He also said: "Intoxicants are the mother of all evils. Whoever drinks them, Allah will not accept his prayer for forty days. Whoever dies with something of intoxicants in his belly, Allah has forbidden him Paradise."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And obey Allah and obey the Messenger, and beware.﴾ When He prohibited wine and commanded them to avoid it, He urged them to obey Allah and the Messenger, and to guard themselves (against disobedience). ﴿But if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 93:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of this verse is that the Companions said, when the prohibition of wine (khamr) was revealed: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the state of one of us who died while he was drinking wine?" So the verse was revealed. It was also said that they said: "Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr were martyred on the day of Uhud, and both used to drink wine; so what is their state?" So the verse was revealed, and Allah, exalted is He, made clear that there is no blame upon them for what they ate during the time when it was permitted, ﴿when they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good﴾. (In this there is an earlier meaning placed before a later statement of opinions.) First: the meaning of the first clause, "when they fear Allah and believe," is that they fear shirk and believe, that is, they affirm, and do righteous deeds. "Then fear Allah" means: they persist in that God-consciousness. "And believe" means: they increase in faith. "Then fear Allah and do good" means: they fear Allah through excellence in every act of goodness, and every obedient person is one who is God-conscious.

The second opinion: the first taqwa is abstaining from shirk, the second taqwa is abstaining from major sins (al-kaba'ir), and the third taqwa is abstaining from minor sins (al-saghair). These are two well-known opinions regarding the verse. There is a third opinion regarding the verse: that it means "when they feared Allah before the prohibition of wine, then feared Allah after the prohibition of wine." It was said that this is not sound, because His saying "when they fear Allah" is only suitable for the future, not the past, since the particle "idha" (when) refers to the future.

﴿And Allah loves the doers of good﴾. It is related that Qudamah ibn Maz'un drank wine, so 'Umar summoned him to apply the prescribed punishment (hadd). He said: "Does not Allah, exalted is He, say: ﴿There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten﴾?" 'Umar said: "You have erred in the interpretation; indeed He said: ﴿when they fear Allah and believe﴾, and you did not fear Allah in refraining from what was forbidden."

It is also related that: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited this verse, then Ibn Mas'ud said: 'And which of us is among these?!'"

The Qur'an's words: "O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game which your hands and your spears can reach..."

Translation:

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game﴾, meaning: Allah will test you with something of the game. The benefit of the trial and testing is the manifestation of the obedient from the disobedient; otherwise He has no need for the trial. The cause of this was that when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) arrived at al-Hudaybiyah with his Companions, and they were in the state of ihram, the game and wild animals came close to them, so they intended to take them; then this verse was revealed.

﴿Which your hands can reach﴾, meaning: among the small game. ﴿And your spears﴾, meaning: from the large wild animals. Mujahid said: ﴿Which your hands can reach﴾ means the chicks and the eggs, ﴿and your spears﴾ means the large game.

﴿That Allah may make evident who fears Him unseen﴾. It was said: its meaning is that Allah may know who fears Him unseen, so that He deals with them as one deals with someone who seeks knowledge in order to act upon it, a manifestation of justice. And it was said: its meaning is that He may see who fears Him unseen. And His saying ﴿who fears Him unseen﴾ means that one fears Allah while not seeing Him. ﴿Whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram (ihram: the sacred state of pilgrimage entered into by a pilgrim)﴾. The occasion of this was that a man called Abu al-Yusr charged at a wild ass and killed it while he was in the state of ihram, and so the verse was revealed: ﴿Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾. The word "hurum" (in the state of sanctity) may derive from ihram, or from entering the Sacred Precinct (haram). It is said: "ahrama" when one has tied the ihram, and "ahrama" when one has entered the Sacred Precinct. It is also said of one who has entered the Sacred Month: "muhrim".

﴿And whoever of you kills it intentionally﴾: the mention of the case of intention is to explain the expiation (kaffarah), and the scholars differed. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the expiation for game is not obligatory for killing by mistake; it is restricted to intentional killing, and Dawud (al-Zahiri) also said this.

All the rest of the scholars hold that it is obligatory in both cases. Al-Zuhri said: for the one who kills intentionally it is by the Book, and for the one who kills by mistake it is by the Sunnah.

﴿then its compensation is the like of what he killed from the livestock﴾. Al-A'mash recited "fa-jaza'uhu mithlu ma qatala min al-na'am" (with the first word in the nominative, as "fa-jaza'uhu"). The well-known readings are two: "fa-jaza'un mithlu" with the word "jaza'" in the genitive construct (idafah), and some read "fa-jaza'un mithlun" with tanwin on "jaza'" and the "l" of "mithl" in the nominative. The meaning of both is one. Likeness is taken into account in the compensation: so for what he kills, its like from livestock is obligatory, by resemblance. Thus for the ostrich a camel is obligatory; for the oryx (arwa) a cow; for the bird, the hyena and the dove a sheep; for the hare an 'anaq (a young female goat); for the jerboa a jafrah (a young goat weaned from milk); and all of this is related from the Companions.

﴿judged by it two just men among you﴾: this is evidence for the permissibility of ijtihad (independent juristic reasoning) in rulings. ﴿as an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾: accusative as a specification (tamyiz). His saying "reaching the Ka'bah" requires that the offering be given within the Sacred Precinct, distributed among the poor of the Sacred Precinct, and this is what is obligatory. ﴿or an expiation of feeding the needy﴾: this means that the like from livestock is valued in dirhams, and with the dirhams food is bought for the needy; this is the view of al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifah said that the killed game is always to be valued. ﴿or its equivalent in fasting﴾: 'Asim al-Jahdari and Talhah ibn Musarrif recited "aw 'idlu dhalika" with a kasrah on the 'ayn. Then some said: there is no difference between them, and its meaning is "like". But al-Farra' distinguished between them, saying: "al-'adl" (with kasrah) is the like of the same kind, and "al-'adl" (with fathah) is the like of a different kind. It has also been said: "al-'adl" with fathah is the like, and "al-'idl" with kasrah is the load; the first is more correct. Fasting the equivalent is that one fasts one day for each mudd (a measure of grain), and it is said two days. Then, is this by choice (takhyir) or by order (tartib)?

Al-Sha'bi and al-Nakha'i, and it is a narration from Mujahid, said: it is by order. Others said, and Ibn 'Abbas held this view: it is by choice, because He said: ﴿or an expiation of feeding the needy or its equivalent in fasting﴾, and the word "or" indicates choice.

﴿that he may taste the consequence of his deed﴾, that is, the severity of his act. ﴿Allah has pardoned what has passed﴾, meaning: in the time of pre-Islamic ignorance (jahiliyyah). ﴿But whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him, and Allah is Mighty, Owner of Retribution﴾.

The scholars differed concerning one who intentionally kills game a second time: is the expiation obligatory for him a second time or not? Ibn 'Abbas said: it is not obligatory, and it is said to him: "You have erred, and Allah will take retribution from you." But the majority of scholars hold that the expiation is obligatory a second time. His saying ﴿Allah will take retribution from him﴾ means: in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 96:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food﴾. Umar and Ali said: "The game of the sea is what is caught from it, and its food is what it casts up (on the shore)." This is also a report from Ibn Abbas. There is another report from him: that its food is what the water has receded from (i.e., what remains on dry land after the water withdraws). Mujahid said: "Its game is the fresh (tari), and its food is the salted (māliḥ)." This is also related from Ibn Abbas. ﴿As a provision for you﴾, i.e., a benefit for you. ﴿And for the travelers﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "As a provision for you" is addressed to the people of the villages (qura), and "the travelers" are the people of the cities (amsar). Mujahid said: "The travelers" are those on journeys (al-musafirun).

﴿And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾. The hunting is forbidden to the one in ihram, and we have already mentioned this. ﴿And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered﴾.

The scholars differed concerning the game of the land that is lawful (halal) to the one in ihram: whether it is permitted for him to eat from it? Umar and Uthman said: it is permitted. Most of the jurists adopted this view. Ali and Ibn Abbas said: it is not permitted, and a group of the Successors (tabi'un) also held this view.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House,﴾ Tha'lab, Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya, said: It was only named Ka'bah because of its squareness (tarbi'uha). ﴿The Sacred House﴾ is the Ka'bah. In a report: "Indeed Allah, exalted is He, made Makkah sacred since He created the heavens and the earth." ﴿A means of sustenance (qiyaman) for the people.﴾ Al-qiyam and al-qiwam are one and the same. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Your wealth which Allah has made for you a means of sustenance (qiyaman)﴾, meaning: a support (qiwaman) for your livelihoods. And a poet said, praising the Prophet:

(And we bear witness that you are the servant of the King, you came with a law and a religion that is upright.) ﴿For the people, and the Sacred Month, and the offerings, and the garlands. That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of everything.﴾

He meant by this: the Sacred House is a support for the people in their religion and their livelihoods. As for religion, it is because the rites and the Hajj are established by it. As for livelihoods, it is because the people of the Sanctuary (ahl al-Haram) were safe from the people of raiding (ahl al-ghara), to the extent that some of them would raid others, yet they would not touch the people of the Sanctuary, and they would say: "They are the People of Allah."

﴿And the Sacred Month﴾: he meant by it the category of the sacred months, which are four months: three consecutive and one single, as has been mentioned before. The meaning is that Allah made the Sacred Month a support for the people, in which they are safe from fighting, for they would refrain from killing and fighting during the sacred months.

﴿And the offerings and the garlands﴾: we have already explained how the offerings and the garlands are, and their being a support for the people is that they were safe by garlanding the offering, and the people of the Sanctuary would make their living through the offerings and the garlands.

﴿That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of everything.﴾ If someone says: What is the connection of this with what preceded in the verse? Al-Mubarrad, Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid, said: Its meaning is: that He inspired them with that reverence, and that they should not molest the people of the Sanctuary; so He thereby made clear in the verse the arrangement concerning the people of the Sanctuary. He said: "That is so that you may know that all of that is by My knowledge and My inspiring them."

Al-Zajjaj said: [It has already preceded] in this surah that Allah, exalted is He, gives information about the unseen and reveals secrets, such as His saying: ﴿Listeners to falsehood, listeners to another people who have not come to you﴾, and such as His informing about their distorting the Books, and the like; so His saying: ﴿That is so that you may know that Allah knows what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾ refers back to that.

God the Exalted says: ﴿Know that Allah is severe in punishment, and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

And in a report (khabar): "If the believer knew what Allah has of punishment, no one would hope for His Paradise; and if the disbeliever knew what Allah has of mercy, no one would despair of His Paradise."

Qur'an 5:99 is quoted within the commentary: "﴿Upon the Messenger is only the conveyance (of the message), and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾"

His statement: "﴿Upon the Messenger is only the conveyance (of the message), and Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.﴾" — its meaning is well known.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 100:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: The evil and the good are not equal﴾. Al-Suddi said: It means the disbeliever and the believer. Others said: The evil (al-khabith) is the unlawful (al-haram), and the good (al-tayyib) is the lawful (al-halal). In a report: "The payment of the soothsayer (hulwan al-kahin) is evil (khabith), and the wages of the prostitute (mahr al-baghi) are evil (khabith)," meaning: unlawful. ﴿Even if the abundance of the evil pleases you﴾: its meaning is, even if it delights you.

﴿So fear God, O people of understanding, that you may prosper﴾. It is said in a proverb: The unlawful comes in bulk (jazfan), and the lawful comes as sustenance (qut). And it is related from Abu Hurayrah that he said: "A dirham of lawful wealth is better than a hundred thousand [dirhams] or more of unlawful wealth."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were disclosed to you, would distress you﴾. The occasion of revelation of the verse: the Companions asked the Prophet excessively until he became angry, stood up to deliver a sermon, and said: "You will not ask me about anything in this place of mine except that I will inform you of it." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is my father?" He was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ḥudhafa al-Sahmi, and there was talk about his lineage. When he asked, "Who is my father?", the Prophet, upon him be blessings and peace, said: "Your father is Ḥudhafa." Then another man stood up and said: "Who is my father?" He was attributed to someone other than his father, as if he were of illegitimate birth. Another man asked: "Where will I be tomorrow?" He said: "In the Fire." Another man stood up and said: "Where will I be tomorrow?" He said: "In Paradise." So they wept. ʿUmar said: "Cover us, O Messenger of Allah, for we are people recently come from the Jahiliyya (the Age of Ignorance)." He went down on his knees and said: "We are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion." And the verse was revealed.

Abu al-Bakhtari narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "When the saying was revealed: ﴿And Allah has a right over the people to visit the House﴾, a man stood up and said: 'Is it every year, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'No. And if I had said yes, it would have become obligatory, and you would not have been able to bear it.' Then he said: 'Leave me what I leave you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. So what I command you, do from it as much as you are able; and what I forbid you, refrain from it.'" And the verse was revealed.

﴿And if you ask about them when the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be disclosed to you﴾. Its meaning: if you are patient until the Qur'an is revealed, you will find in it the explanation of what you need. ﴿Allah has pardoned you concerning them, and Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 102:

﴿Qad sa'alaha qawmun min qablikum thumma asbahu biha kafirin﴾ (“A people before you indeed asked such questions, and then they became disbelievers because of them.”)

Some of them said: It refers to the people of the table (ashab al-ma'idah), who asked for the table (al-ma'idah) and then disbelieved.

Others said: It refers to the people of Salih, who asked for the she-camel (al-naqah), and then disbelieved in it.

Others said: It refers to the disbelievers in the Jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam), who asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to make al-Safa into gold.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah has not instituted any bahirah, nor sa'ibah, nor wasilah, nor ham.﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Their question that preceded concerned these customs, and this verse is an explanation that answers what they asked.

Ibn 'Abbas, explaining these four customs, said:

As for the bahirah: it is a she-camel which, when she had given birth to five offspring, they would slit her ear, leave her alone, not burden her with work, and not prevent her from grazing. It was named bahirah from "bahr," which means splitting. Then they looked at her fifth offspring: if it was a male, they slaughtered it and only the men ate it, not the women; if it was a female, they left it like its mother; and if it was stillborn, both men and women ate it. This is the meaning of the bahirah.

As for the sa'ibah: a man from the people of the Jahiliyyah, when someone of his was sick, or a relative of his was absent, would say: "If Allah returns my absent one, or if Allah cures my sick one, then this she-camel of mine is a sa'ibah." Then he would let her loose to go wherever she wished. Or he would say: "If such-and-such happens, then my slave is freed as a sa'ibah," meaning without any walā' (patronage) or inheritance. This is the meaning of the sa'ibah.

As for the wasilah: it was among the sheep. When a ewe had given birth to seven offspring, they looked at the seventh birth: if it was a male, they slaughtered it and only the men ate it, not the women; if it was a female, they left it; and if it was stillborn, both men and women ate it. If it was a male and a female together in one birth, they left both and said: "She has joined her brother." This is the wasilah.

As for the ham: some of them, when a she-camel gave birth to ten offspring, would leave her, not ride her, and say: "Her back has been protected (ḥamā ẓahruhā)." Likewise, if the offspring of her offspring was ridden, they would say: "Her back has been protected," and leave her. Sometimes they would leave her for their idols, as will come in Surat al-An'am. This is the ham. These were customs that the people of the Jahiliyyah established by their own opinions, and the Law came to abolish them. It has been authentically narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "I saw the Fire, and I saw in it 'Amr ibn Luhayy dragging his intestines in the Fire." He was the first to set loose the sawa'ib.

﴿But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them do not reason.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 104:

﴿When it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down and to the Messenger,"﴾ meaning: when they are called to the Book and the Sunnah, ﴿they say, "Sufficient for us is what we found our fathers upon."﴾ meaning: the religion of our fathers is sufficient for us. ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing, and were not guided?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 105:

His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, meaning: saving them from the Fire. ﴿The one who has strayed cannot harm you once you are guided.﴾ If someone says: How can He say "upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves" when we have been commanded to enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong? It is said: Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the verse concerns the Jews and the Christians, meaning: upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; the one among the Jews and the Christians who has strayed cannot harm you once you are guided. So take the jizyah (poll tax) from them, do not confront them, leave them and what they claim, for it will not harm you.

(And from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him): that he delivered a sermon and said: "You recite this verse, ﴿Upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves; the one who has strayed cannot harm you once you are guided﴾, and I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: When you see the wrongdoer, take hold of his hands, or else Allah will soon encompass you with punishment.") And from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said regarding this verse: "Enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong; if it is accepted from you, that is well, and if it is rejected, [then] upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves." [This is refuted by] what was narrated from Abu Umayyah al-Shaybani, who said: "I asked Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, saying: Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Upon you is [the responsibility for] yourselves﴾, and we have been commanded to enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong. He said: You have asked about it one who is informed. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when this verse was asked about, say: Enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong; but when you see avarice obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person pleased with his own opinion, then keep to your own self and leave the affair of the common people." ﴿To Allah is your return, all of you, and He will inform you of what you used to do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 5, verse 106:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, let there be testimony among you﴾. The occasion of the revelation of the verse: that Tamim al-Dari and 'Adi (ibn Badda'), who were Christians, set out for trade, and with them was Badil, the client of 'Amr ibn al-'As, who was a Muslim. He fell ill, and he wrote down what goods he had in a document and placed it among the goods. Then he bequeathed to those two Christians that they should return his goods to his master if he died. Among the goods was a cup (jam) [inlaid with gold] engraved with gold. They betrayed trust regarding that cup and delivered the rest of the goods to his family. They found the document among the goods, so they asked for the cup and found it missing. They questioned 'Adi and Tamim about it, and they denied it, saying: "We do not know," and they swore an oath on it. Then that cup was found with a man in Medina. The man was asked about it, and he said: "'Adi and Tamim gave it to me." So they brought the matter before the Prophet. He insisted on the denial, and they swore an oath on it. 'Amr ibn al-'As and al-Muttalib ibn Abi Wada'a swore that the two had betrayed trust concerning the cup, so the cup was taken. Then Tamim embraced Islam after that and acknowledged that betrayal. This is the story of the verse, and the verse was revealed concerning it.
